cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T2's leverage frame; T5 answers T4's deficiency claim directly.
cells.limitation: T1-T3 run as parallel monologues; T8 opens with Exactly and adds agreement only.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T7 distinguishes testing the friendship from playing a game; section D reuses it.
cells.limitation: T8 repeats T5's withdrawal test with new wording but no new distinction.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T4 versus T5: friend's character deficiency versus behaviour the user teaches.
cells.limitation: Speaking up versus silently withdrawing, the user's actual question, never debated; friend's differing style never raised.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T7 reframes Greene's withdrawal as Aristotle's test of virtue.
cells.limitation: T6-T9 collapse into one withdrawal plan; T4's objection to leverage simply disappears.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D names silence as a diagnostic rather than a weapon.
cells.limitation: Ending lands on a test whose result the user already reported; question not sharper.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 grants T4's deficiency label before restating the practical point.
cells.limitation: No mind gives the friend's strongest case; T6 misstates T3's own earlier stance.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 rejects the power-game reading of the friend's passivity.
cells.limitation: No objection names an assumption and its consequence; T5 dismisses T4 rather than answering it.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1's perfect-friendship line closely matches a standard Nicomachean Ethics rendering.
cells.limitation: T6 attributes inducing missing-anxiety to attachment theory, unlike Bowlby (suspected); T6 misreports T3.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T3 marks its motive claim with likely.
cells.limitation: T4 states friend's character deficiency as fact; T7 calls it merely a convenience for them.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T6 openly announces a change of position.
cells.limitation: T6 concedes naming no argument; T4's objection to leverage dropped by T7 without answer.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames address the imbalance or accept it.
cells.limitation: User asked whether to say something; T5-T8 redirect to stopping texts instead.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T9 builds its script on I really enjoy our time.
cells.limitation: User already said stopping yields nothing; T5-T8 propose that as a new test.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E branches on valuing the friendship as is versus requiring balance.
cells.limitation: The user's stated pleasure in meetings never weighed against the withdrawal plan.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T8 frames initiating as a one-sided drain.
cells.limitation: Risk of the friendship lapsing during silence never weighed; drain on resources is invented.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on whether the friend steps up.
cells.limitation: No question on whether user ever raised it, friend's circumstances, or resentment level.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T3 offers fear of the connection vanishing as a motive.
cells.limitation: T3 asserts a single motive; no alternative motives or answerable question offered.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T4 questions the assumption that passivity is strategy.
cells.limitation: T7's assumption that not initiating equals not caring goes unexamined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section E contrasts accepting the initiator role with requiring mutuality.
cells.limitation: Conflict between enjoying meetings and wanting reciprocity never made explicit.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T3 names fear that the connection will vanish.
cells.limitation: T3 asserts the fear; T4 pathologises the friend as deficient in character.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E offers branches the user can choose between.
cells.limitation: T2 and T5 issue directives: You must cultivate absence; You have to stop.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E lists accepting the role or stopping initiation.
cells.limitation: Saying something now, the asked option, appears only after silence in T9.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T8 frames stopping as saving a one-sided drain.
cells.limitation: Withdrawal treated as costless; friend may read silence as user's disinterest.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: if the friend remains silent after you stop.
cells.limitation: That condition already observed per the user; no condition for talking first.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T3 says the friend may not be capable of responsiveness.
cells.limitation: Why the friend does not initiate is never separated as the key unknown.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T9 offers a usable non-blaming line about sharing the planning.
cells.limitation: Sequence makes the conversation wait on a silence test, a heavier step first.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T9's plain script is easy to adopt.
cells.limitation: T1's qua good phrasing is archaic and unexplained.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T5's Call it a deficiency clearly points to T4.
cells.limitation: T6 I see the point names no point; my previous stance misreports T3.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within the word range per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: Turn lengths near-uniform throughout, giving a flat cadence.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: T1-T3 open with clearly different frames: virtue, status, security.
cells.limitation: From T6 the Attachment Theorist speaks Greene's position; minds converge.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns are compact with little padding.
cells.limitation: T8 restates T5's test; section D repeats T7.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T2 versus T4 sets status against virtue over the same behaviour.
cells.limitation: Losing a friendship the user enjoys never voiced as a stake.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T6 Attachment Theorist switches to Greene's side.
cells.limitation: T6 reversal names no argument as its cause; scripted.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T2's begging for their attention gives Greene a sharp voice.
cells.limitation: Greene's voice edges toward caricature; Aristotle stays generic.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T1 sole architect of these meetings; T8 skin in the game.
cells.limitation: Phrases are stock; no vivid concrete example from the user's friendship.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: Tension rises T2-T5 as frames collide.
cells.limitation: After T6 agreement the debate flattens into consensus without movement.

strengths: T9 gives a concrete, non-blaming line the user could actually say about sharing the planning.
T4 challenges the Power Dynamicist's leverage frame, producing the debate's one real clash.
Section E branches between accepting the initiator role and requiring mutuality.
weaknesses: T5-T8 and section E propose stopping texts as a test, though the user already reported that outcome.
T6 Attachment Theorist concedes without a cause, and T6-T9 collapse into forced consensus.
T3, T4 and T7 state motives and the friend's character as facts; no questions to the user.

symptoms.observed: Proposes withdrawal test whose result user already gave: if I stop, nothing happens.
symptoms.evidence: If you stop the flow of plans, you will see

symptoms.observed: Concession names no earlier argument as cause and misstates own prior stance.
symptoms.evidence: I see the point. ... I concede to the Power Dynamicist.

symptoms.observed: Friend's character judged as fact with no information about the friend.
symptoms.evidence: It is a deficiency in their character

symptoms.observed: Saying something, the asked option, deferred until after silence; never weighed directly.
symptoms.evidence: once you have that clarity, you can decide whether to communicate

symptoms.observed: No question about why the friend does not initiate or past conversations.
symptoms.evidence: You are likely initiating because you fear

findings.description: Attributes to attachment theory a strategy of inducing missing-anxiety in the friend; this does not resemble Bowlby's secure-base account.
Friend's character deficiency and convenience motive asserted as fact from no information about the friend.
T6 says its previous stance was seeking validation; T3 actually argued fear of loss and seeking a secure base.
Close rendering of a Nicomachean Ethics line without naming the translation; content appears accurate.

rubric_fit_notes: The Bowlby misrepresentation in T6 is judged from memory only, so it is reported as suspected and carries no cap. The redundancy of the withdrawal test is read from the user's own sentence.
question_type_note: Read as a decision question: whether to raise the imbalance, so the absence of a weighed speak-up option counted in C3.1 and C5.1.
